question.problem:
Which of the following could be the interior angles of a quadrilateral?

I. $40^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$, $100^{\circ}$, $170^{\circ}$

II. $20^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$, $150^{\circ}$, $140^{\circ}$

III. $30^{\circ}$, $35^{\circ}$, $140^{\circ}$, $175^{\circ}$
question.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's check this for the above three options:

$$
\begin{aligned}{40}^{∘}+{50}^{∘}+{100}^{∘}+{170}^{∘}={360}^{∘}\,✓ \\  &  \\ {20}^{∘}+{50}^{∘}+{150}^{∘}+{140}^{∘}={360}^{∘}\,✓ \\  &  \\ {30}^{∘}+{35}^{∘}+{140}^{∘}+{175}^{∘}={380}^{∘}\,X\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only options I and II could be the angles of a quadrilateral.
